description: Are you looking for a traditional Milanese Panettone that does not look "too classic" on the outside? Do you want to wow your relatives and friends, maybe even those who fancy design packaging? Don't miss the chance to "make an impression" this Christmas: choose "Cosmik", the sweet creation of Italy's Cosmo Bakery. It's a classic Panettone boasting a pretty attractive box. This Cosmik panettone is baked thanks to the mastery in managing and mixing important ingredients which are also hard to handle, such as mother yeast. The answer is simple: Italian tradition.

The four secrets to taste Panettone at its best

우리의 이야기는 1919년에 시작됩니다. 그때 여러분이 현재 안주인 컵케이크로 알고 있는 것을 세상에 소개했습니다. 아마도 스낵 케이크의 역사상 가장 첫 번째이자 가장 중요한 순간일 것입니다. 할아버지를 물어보세요. 그는 거기에 있었습니다. 6년 후, 컨티넨탈 베이킹은 원더 브레드라고 불리는 핫한 작은 아이템과 함께 판매하기 위해 케이크 라인을 추가하고 싶었습니다. 이 새로운 달콤한 간식 라인은 호스티스로 알려졌습니다. 그리고 브랜드가 탄생했습니다. 지미 듀어가 Twinkies를 발명했을 때 대륙은 1930년 스폰지 케이크 금광을 공격했습니다. 두 마리의 니켈로 인기가 급격히 증가했고 곧 Hostess의 베스트셀러 스낵 케이크가 되었습니다. Twinkies는 이후 미국의 아이콘이 되었습니다. 매년 50억 달러가 만들어집니다. 크림 충전재가 많이 있습니다! 1995년 여름, Interstate Bakeries Corporation은 컨티넨탈 베이킹 컴퍼니를 인수했습니다. 이로 인해 고속고시는 미국에서 갓 배달한 빵과 케이크의 최대 도매 제빵사였습니다. 2009년, 고속고는 사랑을 받는 브랜드를 더 잘 반영하기 위해 Hostess Brands, Inc.로 이름을 변경했습니다. 오늘날까지 빠르게 다가가고, 저희는 딩동, 호호스, 도네트와 같은 새롭고 클래식한 간식을 통해 일상의 순간을 작은 축하 행사로 바꾸고 있습니다. 저희 제품 페이지를 방문하시면 맛있는 스낵 케이크 라인에 대해 더 알아보실 수 있습니다. 하지만 저희한테 가장 좋아하는 것을 고르라고 요청하지 마십시오.

description: The Original Jane Parker Classic Light Fruit Cake 16 ounce (1 Pound) Loaf, in a box. Since the late 1930’s, Jane Parker Fruit Cake has been a staple of American families’ holiday traditions. There's something about the rich goodness of Jane Parker Fruitcake that folks just can't resist. That's because Jane Parker Fruit Cake is real, old-fashioned fruitcake, generously filled with more than 2/3 luscious fruits and nuts. Plump, juicy raisins, glazed pineapple, red cherries, and crunchy pecans are just some of the ingredients that make Jane Parker America's favorite fruit cake. Originally a brand of The Great Atlantic and Pacific Tea Company (A&P), Jane Parker Fruit Cake was baked in the 1930's through the 1960's. There was no production for over 4 decades, then, in 2009, Jane Parker Fruit Cake was brought back for the 150th anniversary of A&P. In 2014, A&P ceased production of Jane Parker Fruit Cakes again, and shortly after filed for bankruptcy. It was feared that Jane Parker Fruitcakes would be gone forever. BUT ...... To the delight of Jane Parker Fruit Cake fans everywhere, in early 2017, the Jane Parker Fruit Cake brand, along with all original recipes, was purchased from A&P, and this iconic brand has been brought back to the market, and is now available again! Baked in both Classic (light) and Dark fruitcake styles, Jane Parker is made with all original recipes and ingredients.You'll find Jane Parker Fruitcake a treat for any occasion! Fresh for 12 months at room temp. May be stored under refrigeration for 18 months. Reccomended to keep refrigerated and remove one hour prior to cutting/serving. description:
For those who want to give a special gift: the cake symbol of Easter, by Cova, the great Italian patisserie based in Milan.

Colomba pasquale or colomba di Pasqua ("Easter Dove" in English) is an Italian traditional Easter cake, the counterpart of the two well-known Italian Christmas desserts, panettone and pandoro. The dough for the colomba is made in a similar manner to panettone, with flour, eggs, sugar, natural yeast and butter; unlike panettone, it usually contains candied peel and no raisins. The dough is then fashioned into a dove shape (colomba in Italian) and finally is topped with pearl sugar and almonds before being baked.

In Antonino Cannavacciuolo's pastry lab, ingredients expertly selected for their great quality are skilfully hand-processed to create gastronomic delights. A scrumptious combination of three, 1 pound Jane Parker Fruit Cakes. One Dark, one Bourbon & Rum, and one Classic. Beautifully displayed and presented in an elegant gold gift box. This amazing gift will surely impress. Give someone on your list the Jane Parker “Triple Delight”! Since the late 1930’s, Jane Parker Fruit Cake has been a staple of American families’ holiday traditions. There's something about the rich goodness of Jane Parker Fruitcake that folks just can't resist. That's because Jane Parker Fruit Cake is real, old-fashioned fruitcake, generously filled with more than 2/3 luscious fruits and nuts. Plump, juicy raisins, glazed pineapple, red cherries, and crunchy pecans are just some of the ingredients that make Jane Parker America's favorite fruit cake. Originally a brand of The Great Atlantic and Pacific Tea Company (A&P), Jane Parker Fruit Cake was baked in the 1930's through the 1960's. There was no production for over 4 decades, then, in 2009, Jane Parker Fruit Cake was brought back for the 150th anniversary of A&P. In 2014, A&P ceased production of Jane Parker Fruit Cakes again, and shortly after filed for bankruptcy. It was feared that Jane Parker Fruitcakes would be gone forever. BUT ...... To the delight of Jane Parker Fruit Cake fans everywhere, in early 2017, the Jane Parker Fruit Cake brand, along with all original recipes, was purchased from A&P, and this iconic brand has been brought back to the market, and is now available again! Baked in both Classic (light) and Dark fruitcake styles, Jane Parker is made with all original recipes and ingredients.You'll find Jane Parker Fruitcake a treat for any occasion! Fresh for 12 months at room temp. May be stored under refrigeration for 18 months. Reccomended to keep refrigerated and remove one hour prior to cutting/serving.

description: Apricot and pear Colomba cake without candied orange peel and with hazelnuts. It belongs to the "Le Antiche Ricette" line, a wide range of hand-packed Colomba cakes featuring elegant wrapping paper. Colomba (Italian for "dove") is a rich and fluffy dove-shaped cake traditionally eaten in Italy at Easter time. It's made thanks to high-quality ingredients and a very long leavening time. After rising, the dough is then baked into a dove-shaped paper baking mould. The Colomba—in its most classic version—features candied orange peel and a sugary glaze on top, which is enriched with pearl sugar and almonds. This specific version is different from the classic one. Instead of candied citrus fruit peel, it features candied apricot and pear cubes. Unlike the classic colomba, this colomba has a top glaze with hazelnuts (instead of almonds.) Natural yeast is the secret of Vergani's excellent Colomba cakes. Even today, Vergani's pastry chefs use the natural sourdough starter created by founder Angelo Vergani in the past. They keep it tied in a cloth, and they refresh it 3 times a day, every day, as the true Milanese tradition dictates, for over seventy years. It takes them a good 3 days to make a colomba cake. And a brand was born. Continental hit the sponge cake gold mine in 1930 when Jimmy Dewar invented Twinkies. At two for a nickel, popularity skyrocketed and it soon became Hostess’ best-selling snack cake. Twinkies have since become an American icon. Half a billion are made each year. That’s a lot of creme filling! In the summer of 1995, Interstate Bakeries Corporation acquired Continental Baking Company. This made Interstate the largest wholesale baker of fresh delivered bread and cake in the United States. In 2009, Interstate changed its name to Hostess Brands, Inc., to better reflect our beloved brands. Fast forward to present day, and we’re continuing to turn everyday moments into small celebrations with a variety of new and classic treats like Ding Dongs, Ho Hos and Donettes, just to name a few. Mediterranean scents and flavours make this particular version of Colomba cake stand out. The delicate dough, prepared with flour, natural sourdough, butter and fresh egg yolk, is filled with a fragrant limoncello cream. It contains candied lemon peels instead of the usual candied orange peels, and it's frosted with a sugary glaze. Colomba (Italian for "dove") is a rich and fluffy dove-shaped cake traditionally eaten in Italy at Easter time. It's made thanks to high-quality ingredients and a very long leavening time. After rising, the dough is then baked into a dove-shaped paper baking mould. The Colomba—in its most classic version—features candied orange peel and a sugary glaze on top, which is enriched with pearl sugar and almonds. Natural yeast is the secret of Vergani's excellent Colomba cakes. Even today, Vergani's pastry chefs use the natural sourdough starter created by founder Angelo Vergani in the past. They keep it tied in a cloth, and they refresh it 3 times a day, every day, as the true Milanese tradition dictates, for over seventy years. It takes them a good 3 days to make a Colomba cake. Colomba (Italian for "dove") is a rich and fluffy dove-shaped cake traditionally eaten in Italy at Easter time. It's made thanks to high-quality ingredients and a very long leavening time. After rising, the dough is then baked into a dove-shaped paper baking mould. The Colomba—in its most classic version—features candied orange peel and a sugary glaze on top, which is enriched with pearl sugar and almonds. Natural yeast is the secret of Vergani's excellent Colomba cakes. Even today, Vergani's pastry chefs use the natural sourdough starter created by founder Angelo Vergani in the past. They keep it tied in a cloth, and they refresh it 3 times a day, every day, as the true Milanese tradition dictates, for over seventy years. It takes them a good 3 days to make a Colomba cake. description: Soichi Ohta, founder of Hawaii Candy, learned the craft of making Senbei (Japanese tea cookies) during the early 1930's as an apprentice in Japan. With his newfound trade, Soichi and his wife Kinuyo opened a neighborhood factory and retail store in 1933. In 1941, Soichi purchased Nakano Candy Factory and renamed his company Ohta Candy Factory. He relocated to Nuuanu Avenue and developed the red coconut balls. He also made all different flavors of candies including cinnamon balls, lemon drops, chestnut drops, and fish shaped candy. In 1954, he purchased what is now known as Hawaii Candy. With purchase of the company came the machines used to make candy. He had two locations, one on Liliha Street which sold Senbei and candy , the other on Nuuanu sold candy only. Hawaii Candy's manufacturing and distribution facility is currently situated near the Honolulu International Airport. Preserving the recipes and maintaining the quality of its products has always been a priority at Hawaii Candy. Although the name Senbei has since been changed to wafer cookies for marketing purposes, the finest and freshest ingredients are still used. Hawaii Candy, serving The Islands since 1933.

description:
The recipe
The art of doing things well: "If we didn't believe in the Goodness of Milan, we wouldn't still be making our products here, in the middle of a city whose greatest strength lies in having such a variety of things and people blending together in a unique mix, like the ingredients of our cakes." Leavened dough, butter, fresh eggs, sugar and candied fruit. The secret is all here. Or almost. To the artisanal touch of the old times Tre Marie brings an insistence on ingredients of incomparable quality, such as prized cubes of Sicilian orange rind.
The ingredients are carefully added in a slow process, starting with hours and hours of leavening and sealed with a rich and crunchy glaze of egg white, sugar and almond or hazelnut flour, garnished with whole almonds and nib sugar. The long and gradual cooling gives this leavened cake unparalleled fragrance and keeps its fluffy structure intact. Our Bakery is all this - complex know-how applied hour after hour and constant control of the whole process, for a cake that is born of slowness, a quality loved by a tradition-loving Milan that not many know.
Because it's only with slowness that certain details come to life, flower and grow, like leavened dough. To do things well, it takes the time it takes. Which also goes for enjoying them.

Colomba pasquale or colomba di Pasqua ("Easter Dove" in English) is an Italian traditional Easter cake, the counterpart of the two well-known Italian Christmas desserts, panettone and pandoro. The dough for the colomba is made in a similar manner to panettone, with flour, eggs, sugar, natural yeast and butter; unlike panettone, it usually contains candied peel and no raisins. The dough is then fashioned into a dove shape (colomba in Italian) and finally is topped with pearl sugar and almonds before being baked.

description: The Original Jane Parker Classic Fruit Cake 72 ounce (4.5 Pound) Ring, in a Box. Since the late 1930’s, Jane Parker Fruit Cake has been a staple of American families’ holiday traditions. There was no production for over 4 decades, then, in 2009, Jane Parker Fruit Cake was brought back for the 150th anniversary of A&P. In 2014, A&P ceased production of Jane Parker Fruit Cakes again, and shortly after filed for bankruptcy. It was feared that Jane Parker Fruitcakes would be gone forever. BUT ...... To the delight of Jane Parker Fruit Cake fans everywhere, in early 2017, the Jane Parker Fruit Cake brand, along with all original recipes, was purchased from A&P, and this iconic brand has been brought back to the market, and is now available again! description: The Original Jane Parker Classic Fruit Cake 72 ounce (4.5 Pound) Ring, in a Box. Since the late 1930’s, Jane Parker Fruit Cake has been a staple of American families’ holiday traditions. There's something about the rich goodness of Jane Parker Fruitcake that folks just can't resist. That's because Jane Parker Fruit Cake is real, old-fashioned fruitcake, generously filled with more than 2/3 luscious fruits and nuts. Plump, juicy raisins, glazed pineapple, red cherries, and crunchy pecans are just some of the ingredients that make Jane Parker America's favorite fruit cake. Originally a brand of The Great Atlantic and Pacific Tea Company (A&P), Jane Parker Fruit Cake was baked in the 1930's through the 1960's. There was no production for over 4 decades, then, in 2009, Jane Parker Fruit Cake was brought back for the 150th anniversary of A&P. In 2014, A&P ceased production of Jane Parker Fruit Cakes again, and shortly after filed for bankruptcy. It was feared that Jane Parker Fruitcakes would be gone forever. BUT ...... To the delight of Jane Parker Fruit Cake fans everywhere, in early 2017, the Jane Parker Fruit Cake brand, along with all original recipes, was purchased from A&P, and this iconic brand has been brought back to the market, and is now available again! Baked in both Classic (light) and Dark fruitcake styles, Jane Parker is made with all original recipes and ingredients.You'll find Jane Parker Fruitcake a treat for any occasion! Fresh for 12 months at room temp. May be stored under refrigeration for 18 months. Reccomended to keep refrigerated and remove one hour prior to cutting/serving. This Classic (light) fruit cake is prepared faithfully to the original recipe, and proudly baked in the USA. Great for larger gatherings or as a hostess gift, corporate gift, or just to gift to yourself, this cake serves 24-36. Enjoy!

description:
The recipe
The art of doing things well: "If we didn't believe in the Goodness of Milan, we wouldn't still be making our products here, in the middle of a city whose greatest strength lies in having such a variety of things and people blending together in a unique mix, like the ingredients of our cakes." Leavened dough, butter, fresh eggs, sugar and candied fruit. The secret is all here. Or almost. To the artisanal touch of the old times Tre Marie brings an insistence on ingredients of incomparable quality, such as prized cubes of Sicilian orange rind.
The ingredients are carefully added in a slow process, starting with hours and hours of leavening and sealed with a rich and crunchy glaze of egg white, sugar and almond or hazelnut flour, garnished with whole almonds and nib sugar. The long and gradual cooling gives this leavened cake unparalleled fragrance and keeps its fluffy structure intact. Our Bakery is all this - complex know-how applied hour after hour and constant control of the whole process, for a cake that is born of slowness, a quality loved by a tradition-loving Milan that not many know.
Because it's only with slowness that certain details come to life, flower and grow, like leavened dough. To do things well, it takes the time it takes. Which also goes for enjoying them.

title: Augusta Classic Panettone from Italy
bullet_point: [Authentic Italian Tradition]
description: Augusta Classic Panettone - Gorgeous Blue HatBox Augusta Panettoni was started in 1945 in Milan by a master pastry chef, custodian of the traditional "Panettone Milano" recipe. Today, as then, the master bakers at Augusta are the custodians of the secret of the special leavening agent, which it mix with the best butter in Europe, exquisite candied fruits and the best quality raisins, together with other first choice ingredients, in order to gives life to this delicious 1kg Classic Panettone. The dough is left to rise naturally, then cooked slowly and carefully and allowed to cool for a full twelve hours, giving the cake its unique taste and flavour. Now crafted in Saronno, north of Milano, in Lombardia. A holiday tradition for those who grew up in Italy or in Italian-American households. Classic with candied orange peel and raisins. Panettone dough rises over several days to achieve the soft yet stranded texture. This long curing of the dough, with the addition of dried or candied fruit brings forth a wonderful texture and fragrance. Panettone is served for dessert, often with trays laden with cookies, torrone and panforte. Some prefer it on the table at brunch. Later in the season, use the last of it for the best French Toast you have ever had. This panettone is moist and sweet, crafted in Italy by artisan bakers. Slice into wedges to serve. Ingredients: Wheat flour, candied orange, citrus, lemon peels; eggs, sultanas, butter, sugar, natural yeast, egg yolk, emulsifier, flavorings, cocoa butter, salt. May contain nuts and soy. Store in a cook dry place.

At two for a nickel, popularity skyrocketed and it soon became Hostess’ best-selling snack cake. Twinkies have since become an American icon. Half a billion are made each year. Plump, juicy raisins, glazed pineapple, red cherries, and crunchy pecans are just some of the ingredients that make Jane Parker America's favorite fruit cake. At two for a nickel, popularity skyrocketed and it soon became Hostess’ best-selling snack cake. Twinkies have since become an American icon. Half a billion are made each year. In 2009, Interstate changed its name to Hostess Brands, Inc., to better reflect our beloved brands. تبدأ قصتنا في عام 1919. هذا هو عندما تم إدخال العالم إلى ما تعرفه الآن باسم هوستس كاب كيك. ربما تكون اللحظة الأولى والأكثر أهمية في تاريخ كيك الوجبات الخفيفة. فقط اسأل الجد الرائع. كان هناك بعد ست سنوات، أراد كونتيننتال بيكينج إضافة خط من الكعك لبيعها إلى جانب قطعة صغيرة ساخنة كانوا يصنعونها يدعى ووندر بيد. أصبح هذا الخط الجديد من الحلوى الحلوة معروفًا باسم المضيف. ولدت علامة تجارية. حازت القارة على منجم الذهب الإسفنجي في عام 1930 عندما اخترع جيمي ديوار توينكيز. في اثنين من أجل الحصول على نيكل وشعبية أصبحت سريعًا كعكة الوجبات الخفيفة الأكثر مبيعًا لدى مضيفة. لقد أصبحت توينكيز أيقونة أمريكية. نصف مليار مصنوع كل عام. هذا الكثير من حشو الكريم! في صيف عام 1995، اكتسبت شركة إنترستيت بيكيريز شركة كونتيننتال بيكنج. وهذا جعل إنترستيت أكبر خباز بالجملة للخبز والكعك الطازج في الولايات المتحدة. في عام 2009، غيرت انترستيت اسمها إلى شركة هوستس براندز لتعكس العلامات التجارية المحبوبة بشكل أفضل. أسرع إلى اليوم، ونحن نواصل تحويل اللحظات اليومية إلى احتفالات صغيرة مع مجموعة متنوعة من المكافآت الجديدة والكلاسيكية مثل دينج دونجز، هو هوس، دونيتس، على سبيل المثال لا الحصر. يمكنك زيارة صفحة منتجاتنا لمعرفة المزيد عن خطنا اللذيذ من الوجبات الخفيفة. ولكن من فضلك لا تطلب منا اختيار ما تفضله.

우리의 이야기는 1919년에 시작됩니다. 이제 호스티스 컵케이크로 알려진 것을 세상에 소개했을 때입니다. 아마도 스낵 케이크의 역사상 가장 중요한 순간일 것입니다. 할아버지를 물어보세요. 그는 거기에 있었습니다. 6년 후, 컨티넨탈 베이킹은 원더 브레드이라고 불리는 뜨거운 작은 아이템과 함께 판매하는 케이크 라인을 추가하고 싶었습니다. 이 달콤한 간식은 호스티스로 알려졌습니다. 그리고 브랜드가 탄생했습니다. bullet_point: [You might think that it might be really plain but actually it contain these flavor bomb chunk ready to be explore., When you talk about banh pia cake that is one of the traditional dessert Vietnamese cusine that create in Soc Trang, Viet Nam., Pia Cake is a sweet, tender and smelling hand-sized round cake with thin wheat flour crust and fillings made from mung bean, durian, salted egg yolk., There's no better than tasting a piece of Pia cake while sipping ginger tea., Enjoy this delicious Vietnamese Durian cake with your friends and family.]
description: Banh Pia is one of the traditional desserts dishes from Viet Nam and it really related to traditional moon cake but the flour that was use for the pia is different than moon cakes. When you talk about durian moon cakes we all know that is a dessert that was use during the moon festival. To describe moon cakes it have variety of different flavor like banh pia the different between the two popular dessert is the crust of the cake. While Pia cake is really fluffy and smooth and moon cake have a more structure and harder outer shell. What that keep in mind thy are both most love dessert for all Asian eater. The history behind banh pia is back to it original produce place that is Soc Trang in Viet Nam. The process of making banh pia is not easy. Just the ingredients alone have to be high quality and hand picked by the most perfect patch of produce. After ingredients is the process of dough making and forming. The difficult thing is that this cake is build by layer, this is why you have that the dough goes from crispy to soft when you bite in the cakes. The two layer is wet dough use tapioca starch, wheat flour, oil and dry dough you need wheat flour, sugar, baking soda and oil. Banh pia is what Soc Trang people call it or pia cake have variety of different flavor there are fifty to be exact from durian, taro, even custard, and mung bean each flavor give you different feeling. All these filling are really hard to combine with other like durian due to it strong smell and quite over power but it a perfect combination with banh pia cake. Durian is originally found in Malay and people from there usually call it as king of fruit due to it appearance and the strong creamy like butter taste but exchange to that is the strong smell.

Since the late 1930’s, Jane Parker Fruit Cake has been a staple of American families’ holiday traditions. There's something about the rich goodness of Jane Parker Fruitcake that folks just can't resist. That's because Jane Parker Fruit Cake is real, old-fashioned fruitcake, generously filled with more than 2/3 luscious fruits and nuts. Plump, juicy raisins, glazed pineapple, red cherries, and crunchy pecans are just some of the ingredients that make Jane Parker America's favorite fruit cake. Originally a brand of The Great Atlantic and Pacific Tea Company (A&P), Jane Parker Fruit Cake was baked in the 1930's through the 1960's. There was no production for over 4 decades, then, in 2009, Jane Parker Fruit Cake was brought back for the 150th anniversary of A&P. In 2014, A&P ceased production of Jane Parker Fruit Cakes again, and shortly after filed for bankruptcy. It was feared that Jane Parker Fruitcakes would be gone forever. BUT ...... To the delight of Jane Parker Fruit Cake fans everywhere, in early 2017, the Jane Parker Fruit Cake brand, along with all original recipes, was purchased from A&P, and this iconic brand has been brought back to the market, and is now available again! Baked in both Classic (light) and Dark fruitcake styles, Jane Parker is made with all original recipes and ingredients.You'll find Jane Parker Fruitcake a treat for any occasion! kendal mint cake is both a tasty treat and a life-saving functional energy candy. Not caffeinated, but packed with glucose and sugar making it a great accompaniment on hikes, bike rides, camping trips, and so on.

kendal mint cake is:

  • a must have for any survival or ration kit.
  • a standard part of the 24-hour ration pack issued to the irish defence forces!
  • melt in the mouth delicious!

kendal mint cake has been used by:

  • ewan mcgregor and charley boorman in their supplies for their 2004 motorcycle trip around the world in long way round.
  • sir ernest shackleton for the imperial trans-antarctic expedition of 1914?1917.
  • sir edmund hillary while climbing mount everest!

romney's kendal mint cake was the first mint cake to be successfully carried to the top of mount everest on 29th may 1953, this being the first successful expedition to the summit.

romney's were approached by the 1953 expedition to everest to see whether they could supply mint cake to them within 7 days. This had to be packed into high altitude packs for inclusion in the supplies to be sent ahead, hence the need for haste. Fortunately they had sufficient stock to meet their needs, and the staff willingly gave up their sweet ration coupons to comply with the law. Sir edmund hillary and tenzing norgay ate this mint cake on top of everest as they gazed at the countryside far below them. Since then kendal mint cake has become a firm favourite with hikers and climbers.

a member of the successful everest expedition wrote, "it was easily the most popular item on our high altitude ration - our only criticism was that we did not have enough of it."

description: The Original Jane Parker Classic Fruit Cake 48 ounce (3 Pound) Ring, in a Box . Since the late 1930’s, Jane Parker Fruit Cake has been a staple of American families’ holiday traditions. There's something about the rich goodness of Jane Parker Fruitcake that folks just can't resist. That's because Jane Parker Fruit Cake is real, old-fashioned fruitcake, generously filled with more than 2/3 luscious fruits and nuts. Plump, juicy raisins, glazed pineapple, red cherries, and crunchy pecans are just some of the ingredients that make Jane Parker America's favorite fruit cake. Originally a brand of The Great Atlantic and Pacific Tea Company (A&P), Jane Parker Fruit Cake was baked in the 1930's through the 1960's. There was no production for over 4 decades, then, in 2009, Jane Parker Fruit Cake was brought back for the 150th anniversary of A&P. In 2014, A&P ceased production of Jane Parker Fruit Cakes again, and shortly after filed for bankruptcy. It was feared that Jane Parker Fruitcakes would be gone forever. BUT ...... To the delight of Jane Parker Fruit Cake fans everywhere, in early 2017, the Jane Parker Fruit Cake brand, along with all original recipes, was purchased from A&P, and this iconic brand has been brought back to the market, and is now available again! Baked in both Classic (light) and Dark fruitcake styles, Jane Parker is made with all original recipes and ingredients.You'll find Jane Parker Fruitcake a treat for any occasion! Fresh for 12 months at room temp. May be stored under refrigeration for 18 months. Reccomended to keep refrigerated and remove one hour prior to cutting/serving. This Classic (light) fruit cake is prepared faithfully to the original recipe, and proudly baked in the USA. Great for larger gatherings or as a hostess gift, corporate gift, or just to gift to yourself, this cake serves 15-24. Enjoy!

description: Soichi Ohta, founder of Hawaii Candy, learned the craft of making Senbei (Japanese tea cookies) during the early 1930's as an apprentice in Japan. He relocated to Nuuanu Avenue and developed the red coconut balls. He also made all different flavors of candies including cinnamon balls, lemon drops, chestnut drops, and fish shaped candy. In 1954, he purchased what is now known as Hawaii Candy. With purchase of the company came the machines used to make candy. He had two locations, one on Liliha Street which sold Senbei and candy , the other on Nuuanu sold candy only. Colomba pasquale or colomba di Pasqua ("Easter Dove" in English) is an Italian traditional Easter cake, the counterpart of the two well-known Italian Christmas desserts, panettone and pandoro. The dough for the colomba is made in a similar manner to panettone, with flour, eggs, sugar, natural yeast and butter; unlike panettone, it usually contains candied peel and no raisins. The dough is then fashioned into a dove shape (colomba in Italian) and finally is topped with pearl sugar and almonds before being baked.
